mechanism_narrative: The broad and sustained improvement across multiple mobility categories like grocery, transit, and workplaces indicates a general increase in out-of-home activity, which will translate to higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite continued improvements in GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in workplace attendance, as observed in the most recent week, signals a return to office-based work which directly boosts demand for retail and recreation services during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next 14 days following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decrease in residential mobility and an increase in transit usage indicates a strong shift in daily routines away from home and towards public spaces, which will synergistically drive up retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to fall and TRANSIT continuing to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The recent improvement in RETAIL_REC itself, coupled with broader mobility gains, suggests that the metropolitan area is in a phase of easing public health restrictions, which will continue to encourage out-of-home activities and further boost retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an improvement compared to the last 28 days, indicating a reversal or stagnation of policy effects.

mechanism_narrative: Despite some recent improvements, the slight dip in parks mobility in the most recent week suggests a potential cooling of outdoor leisure activities, which could signal a broader, albeit temporary, slowdown in discretionary out-of-home movement, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, despite a week-on-week fall in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-week increase in grocery and pharmacy visits indicates a consistent return to essential out-of-home activities, which often precedes and supports a broader recovery in discretionary spending and retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM showing sustained increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined strong rebound in both workplace attendance and transit station activity signifies a robust return to daily commuting and economic engagement, creating a positive feedback loop that will boost retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week by more than 3 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show concurrent week-on-week rises exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: As people spend less time at home (decreasing residential mobility) and more time at workplaces, a new steady state of out-of-home activity is being established, which will consolidate and slightly improve retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining stable or decreasing and WORKPLACES mobility remaining stable or increasing.
